speaker: You
text: Then... what's this?
Inside your locker is a sheet of paper folded in four. On the outside, it only says: «For you».

speaker: You
text: There's no name. Not mine, not anyone's.

«Hi. I don't know how to start, so I'll say it quickly before I change my mind: I like you.»
«I've liked you for a long time. I like the way you laugh when you think nobody's watching, and how you're kind to everyone even when you don't have to be.»
«I don't expect anything from you. I just wanted you to know. Sorry I didn't sign it: I don't have the courage. Besides, there's someone much better for you, and they're closer than you think.»
«Sorry about the stained paper. I'm so nervous I can barely write. Thank you for reading it.»

text: A LOVE LETTER!? TO ME!?

speaker: You
text: Calm down. Breathe. Let's examine it with a cool head.
The sheet is a piece of a spiral notebook: the edge is roughly torn, and the little holes are half ripped.
The handwriting is large and angular, pressed so hard that it left marks on the paper. At the end, the ink is smeared to the right, as if the hand dragged across the still-wet words.

speaker: You
text: Whoever wrote it is a girl, judging by the «nervous» part. And she didn't want me to know who she is.

speaker: You

text: Then... it wasn't you?

speaker: Naofumi
text: N-no. I'm sorry. But if you give me a chance, I can be someone who truly cares about you.

speaker: You
text: A letter from a stranger... and right in front of me, someone who truly cares about me.

speaker: You
text: Naofumi, thank you for being honest. I'd like to get to know you better.

speaker: Naofumi
text: R-really?

speaker: Naofumi
text: T-thank you! I promise... I promise I'll lend you all the books you want.
They start dating. Naofumi smiles much more than before; she even works up the courage to read her favorite passages aloud to you.
Sometimes, between classes, you remember the folded sheet at the bottom of your backpack. You never found out who wrote it.
ENDING 2 - NAOFUMI
You ended up with Naofumi, who truly loved you, but the letter's author never got an answer. Maybe you should have investigated more carefully...
The sun is going down over the park. You arrive ten minutes early, but Yamada is already there, pacing in circles and muttering to herself.

speaker: Yamada
text: You're late! ... No, wait, you're on time. Whatever!

speaker: Yamada
text: Why the hell did you ask me out? Is this a joke? If it's a joke, I'll throw you in that pond!

speaker: You
text: It's not a joke. I wanted to talk to you about something.

speaker: Yamada
text: A-about what?

speaker: You
text: About a letter.

speaker: Yamada
text: A L-LETTER!? What letter? I don't know what you're talking about!

speaker: You
text: An unsigned letter in my locker. Big, cramped handwriting, with the ink smeared to the right.

speaker: Yamada
text: Lots of people write big! How should I know?

speaker: You
text: Someone who writes with their left hand.
Yamada hides her left hand behind her back. You can still see the ink along its edge.

speaker: You
text: Yesterday, at six ten, Makoto saw you by the lockers.

speaker: Yamada
text: I was there for... for something else!

speaker: You
text: And at five fifteen, you went to the library to ask how to write a letter to someone you like.

speaker: Yamada
text: Damn it! That librarian is going to hear from me!

speaker: Yamada
text: You don't know anything! It wasn't me! It wasn't me, okay!

speaker: You
text: Yamada. It was you. I know it.
Yamada opens her mouth to yell, but no sound comes out. She drops onto the bench, her shoulders slumped.

speaker: Yamada
text: ...Damn it.

speaker: Yamada
text: Fine. It was me. Happy? You can laugh now.

speaker: You
text: I'm not laughing.

speaker: Yamada
text: It's just... you're nice to everyone. And I yell, break things, and scare people.

speaker: Yamada
text: Hiroko is cute, friendly, and has known you forever. I wrote that there's someone better because it's true.

speaker: Yamada
text: That's why I didn't sign it. I thought that if you knew it was me, I'd ruin your chance with her.

speaker: Yamada
text: I'm sorry. It was stupid. Forget the letter and go out with Hiroko. She'll make you happy.

speaker: You
text: Yamada, who told you Hiroko is the best person for me?

speaker: Yamada
text: Nobody! It's obvious!

speaker: You
text: When I read your letter, I almost cried with happiness. I loved every word.

speaker: You
text: You wrote that you like the way I laugh when I think nobody's watching. No one had ever noticed that before. You did.

speaker: You
text: I don't care that you're loud. I like you the way you are. I like that you're kind, even when you hide it.

speaker: Yamada
text: D-do you really mean that?

speaker: You
text: Thank you for the letter, Yamada. And my answer is yes.

speaker: Yamada
text: Idiot... idiot! Now you're going to make me cry...

speaker: Yamada
text: D-don't look at me! Look the other way!

speaker: Yamada
text: So... are we... dating now?

speaker: You
text: If you want to.

speaker: Yamada
text: OF COURSE I DO!! Damn it, of course I do!
You walk home together. Yamada, red all the way to her ears, grabs your hand and doesn't let go the entire way.
From the rooftop, Hiroko watches you cross the courtyard together. She frowns, sighs... and, for the first time, says nothing.
ENDING 3 - YAMADA (GOOD ENDING)
You found the true author of the letter and gave her the answer she deserved.
